timeline.body:
Motivation:

Improve performance for these methods
> ByteBuf copiedBuffer(CharSequence string, Charset charset)
> ByteBuf copiedBuffer(CharSequence string, int offset, int length, Charset charset)
> ByteBuf copiedBuffer(char[] array, Charset charset)
> ByteBuf copiedBuffer(char[] array, int offset, int length, Charset charset)

Modification:

- Add an overload method in `ByteBufUtil` to support write ascii string by offset length param.
- Make `ByteBufUtil.reserveAndWriteUtf8Seq` package visible, because `Unpooled` will call this method without check bounds.
- Optimize `Unpooled.copiedBuffer` methods which write CharSequence or char[]
- Optimize call `ByteBuf copiedBuffer(CharBuffer buffer, Charset charset)` directly without check charset twice.
- Rearrange code.
- Add test case.
- Check bounds for index and length of source data.

Result:

Fixes #10205
Reference PR #10206

reply.body:
> I look the doc about autovectorisation. It is about take element from array by index. Here does not do that.

That doc is just one case of autovectorization (it can happen while writing too) and anyway we perform seq.charAt(i) that inlined could lead to be just an array access (ideally). 

My comment is more re to check what happen on ASM level in different cases before assume that a simple change would perform better just because the JMH bench shows it. The JMH numbers are just numbers, I always suggest to understand what's happening under the hood to be sure what they mean. (Didn't want to be rude, is just a suggestion :) )
@franz1981 , That's fine.  I will do more analysis. Tks for your review.

Help me to understand: the new version in this PR can trigger auto-vectorization here?
Or, are you gonna change this part I have reviewed to make it happen, instead?
